## Real runs, other frameworks (`trainproof epoch`)

Training runs nobody wrote for trainproof, judged by the shipped rules.
The logs are in `evidence/`. Both XTTS rows are the *same run* read by two
independent parsers -- a text log and a binary event file.

| framework | log | format | records | steps | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coqui XTTS v2 | `trainer_0_log.txt` | `coqui` | 2501 | 0..125000 | **FAIL**<br>`TP-DIVERGE`, `TP-THROUGHPUT` |
| Coqui XTTS v2 | `events.out.tfevents.1770764871.InfinityGear.19364.0` | `tfevents` | 1255 | 0..125000 | **FAIL**<br>`TP-DIVERGE`, `TP-THROUGHPUT` |
| Lightning / Fish Speech | `events.out.tfevents.1772206357.InfinityGear.2772.0` | `tfevents` | 82 | 24..2049 | **WARN**<br>`TP-OVERFIT`, `TP-THROUGHPUT` |

## Derived observations

- Coqui XTTS v2: `coqui`, `tfevents` are two independent readers of one run and they agree exactly -- same verdict, same rule set.
- `bad_labels`: comparison reaches **FAIL**, the single-run rules only **WARN**. A single run cannot condemn this one.
- `overfit`: the single-run rules reach **WARN**, comparison only **PASS**. A baseline cannot condemn this one.
- `lr_zero` seed 43 is a FAIL that exactly one rule catches: TP-ZERO-LR. Remove that rule and this run passes.
- `lr_zero`: same verdict in every seed, but not the same rules -- which rule fires is seed-dependent.
- `overfit`: same verdict in every seed, but not the same rules -- which rule fires is seed-dependent.

## Why the zero-LR rule exists

Recorded against v0.3-dev, and still true: `lr_zero` seed 43 evaded the dead-run
rule because batch-order noise faked >5% improvement under lr=0, and it passes
comparison because its losses land near baseline -- the pretrained model never
moved. That drove the total-zero-LR fatality rule: lr=0 on every step means the
optimizer never stepped, so it fails from the lr column itself, immune to loss
noise. The tables above show that rule is still the only thing catching it.
